content.value_statement: Long agent sessions can lose file paths, decisions, and next steps during compression. This skill provides structured methods and probes for durable context retention.
actual_capabilities: Explains anchored iterative, opaque, and regenerative summary approaches.
Defines structured summary sections for intent, files, decisions, state, and next steps.
Recommends compression trigger strategies for long agent sessions.
Describes probe-based evaluation for retained context quality.
Compares compression ratios and quality tradeoffs for coding workflows.
limitations: Does not provide an automated compression engine.
Does not run evaluations or measure model outputs.
Requires project-specific summary sections for best results.
Uses guidance and examples rather than executable integrations.

use_cases.title: Preserve Long Coding Sessions
use_cases.description: Keep file changes, decisions, test status, and next steps available after context compression.

use_cases.title: Design Agent Memory Workflows
use_cases.description: Choose a summary structure and compression trigger that fit a product workflow.

use_cases.title: Evaluate Compression Quality
use_cases.description: Create probes that test whether summaries preserve facts needed to continue work.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Summary
prompt_templates.prompt: Compress this session into sections for intent, files changed, decisions, current state, and next steps.

prompt_templates.title: Choose a Compression Strategy
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare anchored iterative, opaque, and regenerative compression for this task. Recommend one strategy and explain the tradeoffs.

prompt_templates.title: Build Retention Probes
prompt_templates.prompt: Design probe questions that verify whether a compressed summary retained errors, files, decisions, and remaining work.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Compression Failure
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this compressed summary against the original session. Identify missing details that could force re-fetching or cause wrong work.

output_examples.input: A long debugging session must be compressed before the next turn.
output_examples.output: A structured summary lists the original goal, files reviewed, files changed, root cause, test status, and next steps.

output_examples.input: A team needs to know whether compression preserved useful context.
output: Probe questions check original errors, modified files, decisions, and follow-up tasks.
Weak answers reveal which summary sections need stronger retention rules.

output_examples.input: A product team compares compression methods for agent workflows.
output_examples.output: The recommendation favors anchored iterative summaries when file tracking and task continuity matter more than maximum token savings.

best_practices: Optimize for total tokens per completed task, not only tokens per request.
Use explicit summary sections for file paths, decisions, errors, and next steps.
Test summaries with probes before relying on them in long workflows.
anti_patterns: Do not compress away file names, function names, or exact error messages.
Do not regenerate every summary when incremental merging would preserve history better.
Do not judge compression quality only with lexical similarity scores.

faq.question: What does this skill help compress?
faq.answer: It helps compress long AI agent sessions, especially coding workflows with files, decisions, and test state.

faq.question: Does it execute commands?
faq.answer: No. The skill is documentation guidance and examples. It does not include executable scripts.

faq.question: Which compression method does it prefer?
faq.answer: It favors anchored iterative summarization when task continuity and file tracking matter.

faq.question: Can it replace project testing?
faq.answer: No. It helps preserve context, but users must still validate changes in their own environment.

faq.question: How should teams measure quality?
faq.answer: Use probe questions that check retained errors, modified files, decisions, and next steps.

faq.question: Is it useful outside coding tasks?
faq.answer: Yes. The structure can help any long task where decisions and follow-up work must survive summarization.
